question: Which of the following screwdrivers has cross-shaped tips that are unlikely to slip from the cruciform slots in Philips recessed head screws?
solution:
The correct answer is __Cross-recess screwdriver**(Option 1)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Cross-recess screwdrivers__ are specifically designed to fit into cruciform slots in screws.
 
• They are equipped with cross-shaped tips to enhance grip and prevent slipping.
 
• These screwdrivers are widely used for driving screws with Phillips recessed heads.
 
• Cross-recess screwdrivers are preferred in various industries due to their reliability and precision.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Ratchet Screwdriver:**

 
 
• It is a screwdriver with a mechanism that allows the user to turn the handle back and forth to tighten or loosen screws without repositioning.
 
• Primarily used for tasks requiring repetitive screw driving.
 
 
 
• **Offset Screwdriver:**
 
 
• Designed for use in tight spaces where a straight screwdriver cannot fit.
 
• It has a bent handle that allows the user to work at an angle.
 
 
 
• **Stumpy Screwdriver:**
 
 
• Also known as a stubby screwdriver, it is shorter in length, making it ideal for confined spaces.
 
• It is available in various tip types, such as flathead or Phillips.
